rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything on earth for human use in life and death, to enable human creation and a happy life, and made it available to people.
rows.anchor: Hep bunları insanı yaratmak ve yarattıktan sonra mes‘ud yaşatmak için yarattı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general benefit of earthly things does not mean each benefits every person in every way; some can also be harmful.
rows.anchor: bir kısmında mazarrat haysiyeti de vardır

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse grounds the legal presumption of original permissibility: things are usable unless a specific proof establishes prohibition.
rows.anchor: Nüfûs ve ırz u nâmustan mâ‘adâ eşyâda asl olan ibâhadır. Husûsî bir delîl-i hurmet bulunmadıkça ibâha ile amel olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Original permissibility rests on this revealed text, not reason alone; reason by itself leads people to conflicting judgments about what is permitted.
rows.anchor: Bu ibâhanın delili yalnız akıl değil bu nastır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission is granted equally to humanity; people were not created for one another, so one person's life and honor are not another's to use.
rows.anchor: bu ibâha insanların umûmuna ‘ale’s-seviyye yapılmış, insanlar insan için yaratılmamış ve yekdiğerine ibâha edilmemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot dispose of their own life or honor at will, including through suicide or selling themselves; only marriage permitted by God is authorized.
rows.anchor: bir insan kendi canında, ırzında bile dilediği gibi tasarrufa me’zun değildir

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's actions, wealth, and property are protected from others, but may be given or transferred with the owner's consent; contracts and financial dealings rest on this basis.
rows.anchor: Lâkin kendileri için mubah olduğundan rızâlarıyla diğerlerine de terk ve i‘tâ edebilirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life, liberty, honor, intellect, and religion are fundamental rights belonging directly to God; violating them is a major sin, and their default status is inviolability.
rows.anchor: hakkullah olan hukūk-ı esâsiyesindendir ve bunlara taarruz kebâirdendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings were created for worship, not merely for self-directed enjoyment of earthly goods.
rows.anchor: insanlar kendileri için değil Allah’a ubudiyet için yaratılmışlardır

words: ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After preparing the earth for people, God directed His will to heaven, ordered its parts and especially the seven heavens, and thereby supplied further benefits to earth and humanity.
rows.anchor: semâya doğrulmuş, iradesini göklere tevcih etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads “seven heavens” as a partitive apposition to the plural pronoun: the plural form, rather than a singular pronoun, signals parts, individuals, or kinds.
rows.anchor: فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ,”سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ’den bedeldir. Ve bedel-i ba‘z zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage summarizes humanity's pre-life nonexistence, expands the earlier description of earth and heaven as habitation, proves God's lordship, and summons deniers to gratitude and worship.
rows.anchor: nihâyet inâyet ve rahmet-i ilâhiyenin vüs‘ati ile zât ve sıfât-ı ilâhiyeyi münkirlere isbat

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: Şeyh Sa‘dî
rows.claim: Saadi's poem depicts cloud, wind, moon, sun, and sky as serving people so they can obtain their daily bread, expressing the passage's theme of creation serving human benefit.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Sa‘dî merhum Gülistân’ında bu mazmunu şöyle ifade etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are not merely earthly creatures: they have a share in heavenly benefits, but spiritual ascent requires sensing their celestial vocation and knowing God; those sunk in sensual life miss it.
rows.anchor: insan yalnız arzî bir mahluk değildir. O yerlerde daralırsa göklerden intifâ‘a mezundur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence marked by thumma can be rhetorical or rank-based rather than chronological: the account follows human cognition, which begins with the self, then earth, then heaven.
rows.anchor: sonralık, yani ثُمَّ mânası zamânen değil rütbeten, yani ifade nokta-i nazarından bir sonralıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People first know earth through touch and bodily weight, then heaven; God speaks in that order, so the verse's surface order alone does not prove earth was created first.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak da irşâdâtını, idrâk-i beşerin bu cereyânına göre beyan buyurmuştur ki bunu zâhirinden arz semâdan evvel yaratılmış gibi anlamamalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows a literal temporal reading too: although earth was not absolutely created before heaven, the formation of earth as a distinct body could follow earlier heavenly ordering, as 21:30 indicates.
rows.anchor: arz ‘ale’l-ıtlâk semâdan evvel yaratılmış değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a physical account, earth's formation and gravity altered the arrangement of its celestial system, so the seven heavens related to earth would have been ordered afterward; unaffected regions lie beyond them.
rows.anchor: câzibe-i arziyye ile alâkadar olan seb‘a semâvât tesviyesi ve nizâm-ı hilkati arzdan evvel değil, sonra olmak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One astronomy-based proposal counts seven heavens outward from earth through the planetary intervals to beyond Saturn, including Uranus, Neptune, and any planets later discovered within the seventh boundary.
rows.anchor: Arz’dan Zühre’ye kadar bir, Zühre’den Utarid’e iki, Utarid’den Şems’e üç, Şems’ten Mirrih’e yahut yine Arz’dan Mirrih’e dört

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This model is relational to earth and need not imply that earth is the solar system's center; an observer on the sun would count the planetary intervals from there instead.
rows.anchor: bunda mevzû‘-i bahis arzın merkeziyeti değil arza nazaran “semâ” kelimesinin tatbîkidir

rows.speaker: Batlamyus ilm-i hey’etini tâkip edenler
rows.claim: Ptolemaic astronomers counted the Moon as the first planet and Saturn as the seventh, then tried to fit the Qur'anic heavens to that model.
rows.anchor: Batlamyus hey’etini tâkip edenler Kamer’i birinci seyyare saydıklarından ondan başlarlardı ve yedincisi Zuhal’e dayanırdı

rows.speaker: Batlamyus ilm-i hey’eti
rows.claim: Ptolemy's theory assigned each of seven planets a sphere, another sphere to the fixed stars, and an encompassing Atlas sphere whose motion produced daily motion; planetary motion was explained as natural and forced components.
rows.anchor: Seyyârelerde iki hareket görülüyor, bunun biri tabîî ise diğeri her hâlde kasrî olmak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: ulemâ-yı tefsîr ve mütekellimîn
rows.claim: Exegetes and theologians argued that Ptolemy's cosmological theory was not certain and that another cause could explain the motions.
rows.anchor: ulemâ-yı tefsîr ve hatta mütekellimîn de bu nazariyenin yakīnî olmadığını, diğer bir sebebin melhuz olabileceğini söylüyorlardı

rows.speaker: Sâbit b. Kurre
rows.claim: The philosopher Sābit ibn Qurra had already proposed an attraction theory as an alternative explanation.
rows.anchor: Sâbit b. Kurre bir cezb nazariyesini bile dermeyan etmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern astronomy has narrowed its serious work to the solar system, so proposals beyond it remain hypothetical; gravitational theory had no known empirical or inductive counterexample and fits Qur'anic descriptions of unsupported heavens.
rows.anchor: Câzibe-i umûmiye kanunu bugün âdetâ müte‘ârife tavrını almış bir mevzû‘a-i ilmiye olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because gravity is an abstract, almost spiritual concept, he says it would be more serious and wise to conceive it through an angel and connect it directly to divine power.
rows.anchor: bunu bir “melek” kelimesiyle tasavvur etmek ve bizzat kudret-i ilâhiyeye rabt eylemek daha ciddî ve daha hikemî olurdu

rows.speaker: ekâbir-i müfessirîn
rows.claim: Another view makes the star-adorned material cosmos above earth the lowest heaven, with six further heavens beyond it; Elmalılı identifies this as the view of leading exegetes.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın üstünde bütün yıldızların tezyin ettiği maddî âlemin hepsi bir semâdır. Seb‘a semâvâtın birincisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the other heavens are understood as spiritual and intelligible, their correspondence is clearer than a material picture of layered physical space; 37:6 describes the lowest heaven's stars.
rows.anchor: Bunlar rûhânî ve ma‘kul olarak tasavvur edildikleri zaman fezânın ecsâma intibâkı gibi aralarında tıbâk u mutabakat mefhûmu daha bârizdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of the Prophet's ascension also point to spiritual meanings of the heavens.
rows.anchor: Sonra miraç hadislerinde de semâvâtın böyle rûhânî mânalarına işaret vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continually orders the heavens' varied affairs; this ordering is not limited to matter, and after creating earth He specially ordered them and set angels and effects to prepare the world for people.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak her an bunların şu‘ûn-ı muhtelifesini tesviye etmektedir. Ve bu tesviye maddiyâta münhasır değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's eternal knowledge answers doubts that cosmic events are blind chance or that earth and heaven could have been prepared for life in advance; knowledge underlies sciences and the connection of causes and effects.
rows.anchor: Esbâb ve müsebbebât birbirine nasıl merbut olurdu? Fünun nasıl teessüs ederdi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is the product and small copy, perhaps even the great copy, of earth and heaven, created through divine knowledge, power, and encompassing mercy with its means of happiness prepared.
rows.anchor: insanları böyle yüksek bir ilm ü kudretle, böyle şâmil bir rahmetle arz u semânın bir hâsılası, bir nüsha-i suğrâsı ve belki kübrâsı olarak yaratmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should recall these gifts, investigate what was prepared for their benefit, use it in God's way, prepare for the afterlife, and aspire upward because they will return to God.
rows.anchor: bu edvârı, bu nimetleri derhâtır ediniz, rûhunuzun ne gibi ulviyetlere namzet kılındığını düşününüz

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites demanded a direct sight of God before believing Moses; the calamity struck them into a near-death state in which they could only stare, not move.
rows.anchor: kımıldanmaya dermanınız kalmamış, sade bakıp duruyordunuz

rows.speaker: Birçokları
rows.claim: Many understood the phrase to mean they were struck dead while looking, but Elmalılı rejects that reading: the looking is concurrent with the striking, not a state after death.
rows.anchor: Birçokları bunu bakıp dururken yıldırım çarpmıştı, ölmüş idiniz mânasına anlamışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the looking clause as a circumstantial phrase or coordinated event concurrent with the striking; the parallel account calls the event a trembling calamity.
rows.anchor: وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ atfı veya hâli bilhassa böyle bir zehâba meydan vermemek içindir

rows.speaker: Vehb
rows.claim: Vehb reports that they did not die: terror made them tremble so violently that their joints seemed to separate and their backs to break, bringing them near destruction.
rows.anchor: Vehb hazretlerinden rivayeten dahi bunlar ölmemişler, belki o korkunç hâli gördükleri zaman kendilerini öyle bir titreme, bir zangırtı almış

rows.speaker: Vehb
rows.claim: In Vehb's account Moses wept and prayed, God granted relief, and the people's senses returned; verse 56 describes their recovery as revival after death.
rows.anchor: o zaman Hazret-i Mûsâ ağlamış, Rabbine dua etmiş, Cenâb-ı Allah da bir açıklık ihsan eylemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two views place the event either after the killing episode or before it, immediately following the command; Elmalılı leaves the timing open.
rows.anchor: Bu vâkı‘anın zikrolunan katlden sonra mı, veya ondan evvel ve katl emrini müte‘âkib mi olduğu hakkında iki kavil zikrediliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever its timing, the calamity amounted to a people's death and their rescue to a renewed life and great blessing; the cause was refusing faith until they saw God, while release was divine care.
rows.anchor: bu sâ‘ika bir kavmin memâtı mesâbesinde bir musibet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although only a selected group of seventy at the meeting suffered the calamity, the Qur'an attributes the demand, trial, and revival to the whole people, including its later audience.
rows.anchor: bizzat sâ‘ikaya tutulanlar da müntehab yetmiş kişi idi. Böyle olduğu hâlde bu âyette gerek dava, gerek musibet ve gerek ni‘met-i ba‘s

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the collective attribution through shared responsibility in public duties and communal obligations: the community, not an isolated individual, is the relevant subject, and all share its good and bad.
rows.anchor: hukūkullah olan vezâif-i umûmiye mesâilinde, farz-ı kifâye maddelerinde ferd mevzû‘-i bahis değil, yalnız cemaat, nefs-i ümmet mevzû‘-i bahistir

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prior blessings, refusing Moses until seeing God was a grave act of disbelief and ingratitude, and the verse sharply warns about knowledge of God and human spiritual decline or ascent.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya isyan etmek ne büyük bir küfür ve küfrandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual ascent frees sight, heart, and reason from the immediately visible and enables faith in unseen truths; decline narrows them to the senses and refuses anything not seen until disaster arrives.
rows.anchor: insanlar terakki edecekleri zaman nazarları, kalbleri yükselir, idrakleri yalnız gözleri önünde duran mahsüsâta bağlanıp kalmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sensory-only people want to touch and handle their deity; because worship is an innate human law, people unable to draw strength from the unseen seek tangible idols such as a calf.
rows.anchor: Çünkü insanlarda ibadet kānûn-ı fıtrîdir. Bundan kurtulamazlar, fakat ma‘bûd-ı hakīkīyi göremeyince kalblerinden, akıllarından kuvvet alamayınca

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Israelites, shaped by what they had seen in Egypt or their failure to rise spiritually, demanded that Moses show them God as a physical, encompassing object, an impossible demand.
rows.anchor: veya herhangi bir sebeple tekrar sukūt etmiş olmaları dolayısıyla Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They treated God as if He were a bounded body before them, although such an encompassing vision was impossible; the miracles and evidence they had already seen should have sufficed.
rows.anchor: bununla Allah’ı bir cisim gibi karşılarında muhît bir rü’yetle görmek istemişler ki muhal idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strike came as a miraculous punishment and the rescue as a miraculous act of mercy; though they did not see God, they saw a punishment no other deity could produce and learned the importance of faith without sight.
rows.anchor: başka mâbudların yapamayacağı ‘ikābını görerek akılları başlarına gelmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not inherently unseen or impossible to see and can create eyes capable of seeing Him, but present eyes cannot bear Him and sight cannot encompass Him.
rows.anchor: Lâkin ona bu gözler dayanmaz ve görülürse ihâta olunmaz

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human benefit in worldly life lies in believing in God while He is absent from sight, through rational and inward testimony.
rows.anchor: Bizim dünyada fâidemiz ona gıyâbından şehâdet-i akliye ve kalbiye ile inanmaktır
